text:
Maria: Heads-up — p99 for small-gen calls from dedicated-eu2 jumped ~3x since 09:12UTC. Hitting SLOs for a handful of customer routes. Anyone else seeing this?
Sam: Yea, got the alert. Graphs show a sharp step at 09:12, tails concentrated on seq<=64 requests.
Maria: Quick look at the node logs (gputeu2-12) shows repeated `cudaMemcpyAsync stall` and blocks in runtime IO. NIC util on eth1 also looks high.
infra-bot: ALERT: latency_p99_dedicated_eu2 > 500ms for 5m (rule: dedicated_latency_slo)
Rachel: Could be cross-tenant burst — there was a shared-batch deploy around 09:10 that might have warmed big IO.
Kevin: Allocation history: gputeu2-12 hosts 1 dedicated slice (cust-A) + 2 fractional shared slices. preempt_score stayed low. Possible IRQ/affinity shift after the deploy.
Sam: Pulled counters: `ssh gputeu2-12 sudo ethtool -S eth1 | grep "tx_bytes"` shows sustained tx spikes aligned w/ latency jump.
Maria: Paste from runtime around 09:12:
```
[09:12:14] driver: queue_depth=256 stall_count=34
[09:12:14] runtime: kvcache_miss=0.02 cpu_wait=0.6
[09:12:15] nic: tx_bytes_delta=18MB pps=12k
```
Rachel: Proposal: temporarily reroute the affected tenant to warm-dedicated pool for 30m while we do non-disruptive mitigation on the node. Add a routing tag `sli-hit` and bump priority.
Kevin: Two concerns: warm-dedicated pool has very limited spare capacity in eu2 right now, and routing to a different AZ or pool may change egress path and cost for that tenant. Need to check cost impact.
Sam: Alternatively we can soft-carve a slot by marking the tenant slice `qos=high` and toggling preemptible=false for 30m. Quick API call: `PATCH /allocations/{slice_id} { \"qos\": \"high\" }` — this should move the scheduler to prefer non-shared nodes if capacity allows.
Maria: @Kevin are you oncall? Can you take lead on the routing decision?
Kevin: I'm oncall. I'll coordinate. First non-disruptive step: throttle co-tenants' NIC egress on gputeu2-12 using `tc` so we reduce crossflow. If that buys time, we reroute.
Oliver: I can apply a temporary tc filter. Command I'll run: `sudo tc qdisc add dev eth1 root tbf rate 300mbit burst 32k latency 70ms` then targeted `tc filter` for the offending slices.
Rachel: Good — NIC shaping preferred over runtime restart. If shaping fails, we do the warm-dedicated reroute.
Sam: Action plan summary: Oliver -> apply tc shaping on gputeu2-12 (10m). Maria -> create routing override for cust-A to warm-dedicated if shaping doesn't restore p99. Kevin -> monitor p99 and allocation shifts. Sam -> create incident and own escalations.
Sam: Creating incident INC-4721 now.
infra-bot: Incident INC-4721 created by Sam: "dedicated-eu2 p99 spike — potential cross-tenant NIC saturation"
Maria: Thanks all. I'll update after the first 10m check. :thumbsup:
Oliver: Applied tc shaping. Patch log:
```
09:23:02 sudo tc qdisc add dev eth1 root handle 1: tbf rate 300mbit burst 32k latency 70ms
09:23:05 tc filter add dev eth1 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 u32 match ip src 10.40.12.0/24 flowid 1:1
```
Kevin: Seeing preliminary drop in tx_bytes_delta and p99 trending down from 640ms -> 320ms in the last 3m. Still above target but improving.
Maria: If p99 < 300ms in next 10m we keep shaping and close INC-4721 as mitigation-only. If not, we execute reroute to warm-dedicated.
Sam: Noted. I'll keep the incident open and add timeline.
Maria: Update in 10. :eyes:
